title: The Flood as deliberate reset
statement: The ancient flood narratives — Genesis 6-9, Atrahasis, Gilgamesh XI, the Sumerian Flood Story, the Book of the Watchers — share a decision procedure rather than a divine mood: a resolution taken in assembly, sworn and treated as irrevocable, opposed by an internal dissenter, executed with a warned survivor under precise instructions to preserve the seed of living things; and the canon reads the event itself as a deliberate reset of the antediluvian project, with the genetic stock preserved aboard a craft and the human remnant re-established afterwards.

includes: The textual-procedure layer, which is an inferred reading of the sources: assembly decision, oath, dissent (Enki against Enlil; the Atrahasis 'wrong instrument' argument naming targeted alternatives), survivor instructions, seed-preservation formulae

The canonical layer, which is framework: the Flood as a deliberate reset decision within the Council's governance of the Earth project, with the cell-line preserved aboard a staged craft (TBWTT ch. 2), operating within the wider conflict recorded as woh-claim-0008
The cross-tradition convergence of the procedure across the named texts, at the level the project's flood-myths dataset tabulates
excludes: Historicity or dating of a global flood as a geological claim; the record concerns what the texts describe and how the canon reads them
The claim that all two-hundred-plus flood traditions worldwide share the decision procedure; the procedural reading is anchored on the named Near Eastern and Enochic texts
Any reading of the flood as punishment-of-wickedness simpliciter; the record registers the canon's reset framing against it without erasing that the Genesis redaction itself moralizes the event
Mechanism details beyond what the canon states

source_references.locator: Chapter 2 (the Flood; the cell-line preserved aboard a staged craft; the re-establishment afterwards)
ATRA-WOH-II (the decision and the dissent; the 'wrong instrument' argument with named targeted alternatives); ATRA-WOH-III (the warning and the boat)
SB Tablet XI (GILG-WOH-11, in-house digitization): the assembly decision, Ea's warning through the reed wall, the seed of all living things
GEN-WOH-6:5-22 (the resolution and the instructions); 7-8 (execution and subsidence); 9 (the covenant and the never-again oath)
The Book of the Watchers' flood frame: the destruction ordered against the corrupted generation with Noah preserved
The standard critical commentary on the Genesis flood redaction and its Mesopotamian background

alternatives.statement: The shared procedure reflects the documented literary stream Atrahasis → Gilgamesh XI → Genesis; a common source text explains the convergence without a common event.
The narratives are theology of divine judgment and covenant; the procedural texture is narrative convention, not the record of a deliberation.
The traditions preserve memories of separate local inundations, mythologized independently; no single event stands behind them.
The reset reading retrofits a modern engineering frame (staged craft, cell-line) onto texts that carry no such content.

revision_triggers: Source-language review of the in-house Atrahasis, Gilgamesh XI, or Genesis renderings materially changes a procedural observation.
The flood-myths dataset's expansion shows the decision-procedure features do not hold beyond the Near Eastern textual stream, narrowing the claim to literary dependence.
Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0008 is revised or retired.
Public prose begins asserting geological historicity or extending the procedure to all worldwide flood traditions, which this record excludes.
